locator: I q.2 a.3 obj. 1: si unum contrariorum fuerit infinitum, totaliter destruetur aliud
interpretation: The objection opposes evil to God as the contrary of the infinite good his name signifies, so the evil its minor premise asserts ('invenitur autem malum in mundo') is badness, the contrary of good, not a non-evaluative fact such as pain. Read as: the evil premise says of something that it is bad. A critic who restates the premise non-evaluatively ('there is suffering') makes a different argument, which needs a further evaluative premise of its own (for instance O'Connor's 'a loving god would not permit such suffering', itself a moral statement). This bridge is kept apart from O'Connor's classification of badness ascriptions as moral.
